exposure: Genotype of the surrogate mother (C57BL/6J, NOD SCID, BALB/c)
Immunogenetic interaction variants between mother and foetus
outcome: Body composition (body mass, percent of fat)
Innate immune responsiveness (peritoneal macrophage responses, IL-1b reaction to anthrax)
Adaptive immune responsiveness (humoral immune response, serum IgG, H. hepaticus DNA, IgA, IFN-g, TNFa, IL-17, IL-10)
cohort: Offspring (n=171) of C57BL/6J mouse embryos transferred into C57BL/6J, NOD SCID, or BALB/c surrogate mothers were assessed.
finding: C57BL/6J progenies carried by immunodeficient NOD SCID mothers exhibited increased adaptive but decreased innate immune responsiveness compared to offspring carried by immunocompetent mothers, while B6 progenies carried by same-genotype mothers had higher body fat.
mod_finding: All pups were delivered by Caesarean section.
